title: Bumrah Ruled Out of Sri Lanka Tests, Pandya Recovery Drags On Ahead of 2027 World Cup
excerpt: India's pace spearhead Jasprit Bumrah has been withdrawn from the Sri Lanka Test squad due to a persistent left knee injury, while Hardik Pandya remains sidelined with a quadriceps setback.
body:
• Jasprit Bumrah has been ruled out of India's two-Test series against Sri Lanka starting August 15 in Galle due to a persistent left knee injury
  • Hardik Pandya continues rehabilitation at the BCCI Centre of Excellence for a quadriceps injury, with no confirmed return date
  • Auqib Nabi, a 29-year-old Jammu & Kashmir seamer, earns his first senior Test call-up as Bumrah's replacement

India's injury crisis deepened this week as pace spearhead Jasprit Bumrah was formally ruled out of the upcoming two-Test series against Sri Lanka, while all-rounder Hardik Pandya's recovery from a quadriceps setback continues without a clear timeline.

The BCCI confirmed on August 3 that Bumrah, 32, has been withdrawn from the squad after failing to recover from a left knee injury sustained while fielding during the second ODI against England in Cardiff on July 16. He had been included in the 15-member squad subject to a fitness test at the BCCI's Centre of Excellence in Bengaluru, but persistent discomfort led the medical team to advise against his return.

No Risks with Bumrah

"There have been instances in the past where players have been rushed back to cricket, and have broken down. You can't take that risk again. Especially with Bumrah."

— BCCI source, via Times of India

The world's top-ranked Test bowler received an injection in his knee following the England series as part of a long-term fitness plan. The medical team reportedly determined that rushing his return could lead to a longer spell on the sidelines, with the BCCI prioritizing his availability for the Asian Games, the tour of New Zealand, and the Border-Gavaskar Trophy early next year.

Nabi Gets Historic Call-Up

Uncapped fast bowler Auqib Nabi, 29, has been named as Bumrah's replacement, earning his first senior Test call-up. Nabi took 60 wickets in the 2025-26 Ranji Trophy season to help Jammu & Kashmir win their first-ever title, and claimed six wickets in two first-class matches during India A's tour of Sri Lanka in June-July.

He becomes the first cricketer from Jammu & Kashmir to receive a call-up to the senior Test side — a milestone for a region that has historically been underrepresented in Indian cricket.

Pandya's Prolonged Absence

Hardik Pandya's situation remains equally concerning. The pace-bowling all-rounder, who missed multiple IPL 2026 matches due to back spasms, suffered a fresh quadriceps setback just as he was poised to return through the series against Ireland and England. He is currently undergoing rehabilitation at the Centre of Excellence in Bengaluru, with no confirmed return date.

The dual absence of Bumrah and Pandya leaves India without its two most impactful pace options across formats. Nitish Kumar Reddy, considered Pandya's backup, is also sidelined with a quadriceps injury picked up during the third ODI against Afghanistan.

Vihari Questions Commitment

The mounting injury list has drawn pointed criticism. Batter Hanuma Vihari questioned whether India's stars are fully committed to international cricket, noting that Bumrah, Pandya, Nitish Kumar Reddy, and Varun Chakravarthy all played 14 IPL matches but broke down when international duty resumed.

"If these players are unfit and we have to keep changing the combinations before the World Cup, it will become difficult," Vihari said. "Are players motivated enough to play international cricket? Or want to play the IPL for money and fame and take it lightly?"

India's Test Squad for Sri Lanka

India begin the series in Galle on August 15. The updated squad: Shubman Gill (captain), KL Rahul (vice-captain), Yashasvi Jaiswal, Rishabh Pant (wk), Sai Sudharsan (subject to fitness), Dhruv Jurel (wk), Ravindra Jadeja, Kuldeep Yadav, Manav Suthar, Mohammed Siraj, Prasidh Krishna, Gurnoor Brar, Devdutt Padikkal, Saransh Jain, and Auqib Nabi.

With Bumrah absent and the World Test Championship final still in contention, India's pace attack of Siraj, Prasidh Krishna, Gurnoor Brar, and Nabi faces a significant test on Sri Lanka's spin-friendly tracks.
